subject: OptiScale privacy follow-up: PII handling & retention options
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@optiscale.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Foster <jordan.foster@optiscale.com>, Legal Ops <legal@optiscale.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: privacy/retention requirements and next steps

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align with our security and procurement teams: 

- Primary requirement: OptiScale cannot retain any PII or customer-provided text beyond the timeframe required to serve the request. Ideal outcome would be 0-retention for prompt/response pairs at the hosted API layer.
- Residency: EU regional residency is preferred for production but our initial POC can run in us-west if encryption/KMS controls are in place.
- Logging: We need to understand what gets persisted in logs (request bodies, model outputs, KV cache hits, telemetry). If any user-provided data is kept for troubleshooting, we need clear TTLs and redaction options.
- Evidence: please share SOC 2 Type II, encryption-in-transit/at-rest details, and any sample contract language for a retention carveout.

High level ask: can Redwood do a time-limited 0-retention pilot (no persistent request/response logs, ephemeral KV cache) for the POC? If not, what is the shortest achievable retention window and what redaction/PII-detection appliances are available?

We attached our requirements spreadsheet for reference. Proposed next steps from our side: procurement review this week; we aim to have a PO for POC by end of July.

Attachments: [Attachment: optiscale-privacy-requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
OptiScale
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@optiscale.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy/retention requirements and next steps

Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Below is a concise set of options and constraints from our side so you can share with procurement/security: 

Option A — Private deployment (recommended for strict 0-retention)
- Private control plane (VPC) or on-prem package; customer-managed networking + optional HSM/KMS.
- We can configure inference nodes so that request/response payloads are not written to persistent logs. KV cache kept in-memory only.
- Requires Private or Dedicated contract and a short implementation lead time (2–4 weeks for a small PoC).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II available; we can provide redacted reports and a security checklist.

Option B — Hosted API with pilot concession (limited & auditable)
- We can run a time-limited pilot on hosted infra with strict access controls and accelerated purge (short TTL). For hosted we cannot guarantee full 0-persistence by default, but we can implement a shortened retention window (e.g., 7 days) and restrictive role-based access for debugging.
- Additional controls: auto-redaction pipeline for high-risk fields, prefix-only KV caching, and audit hooks to track access.

Option C — Hybrid (dedicated pool + ephemeral logging)
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) with node-level in-memory caching and a strict logging policy; useful if you need throughput guarantees and shorter retention than hosted standard.

Open questions from our side:
- Do you require zero-persistence of the model KV cache specifically, or just request/response logs?
- For EU residency: do you need data-at-rest physically in-region, or would a contractual residency + encryption suffice for the POC?

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I’ll loop in Rishi (security/controls) and Aditya (solutions) to prepare an options deck and a suggested narrow pilot plan (tech design + timeline).
2) If OptiScale is open to Private/Dedicated for the POC, we can scope infra and a tightened commercial term for the pilot (30–60 day concession around retention).
3) Share the specific redaction fields you care about (PII examples) so we can validate the auto-redaction rules.

I’ve attached a short one-pager that summarizes the privacy/retention choices and what evidence we can provide.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-privacy-options.pdf (application/pdf)]

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@optiscale.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Foster <jordan.foster@optiscale.com>, Legal Ops <legal@optiscale.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy/retention requirements and next steps

Thanks Tessa — that is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/legal: 

- For POC we are open to Dedicated if the cost and timeline are reasonable. Priority is no retention of identifiable PII (names, emails, cleartexts) in any persistent log. In-memory caching is acceptable as long as it’s flushed on session end.
- For evidence: can you send your SOC 2 attestation and a short note on KMS/HSM integration? We’ll also need sample contract language for the retention carveout to pass to our Legal Ops.
- Encryption question: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for the POC or only Redwood-managed keys?

Timeline: procurement wants a draft SOW and security appendix by 7/2 to move forward. Can Redwood provide staged deliverables (security checklist now, SOC2 + contract language next week)?

I attached a set of vendor security questions from our security team. Let us know if anything needs clarification.

Attachments: [Attachment: vendor-security-questions.pdf (application/pdf)]

—Alex
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OptiScale POC ask — zero-retention pilot? (deal OPTI-472)

Team —

Quick internal note after the OptiScale thread (summary + proposed approach):

Summary of ask: OptiScale requests a time-limited 0-retention pilot for PII (no persistent request/response logs; in-memory KV cache only) and EU residency for production. They’re willing to run an initial POC in us-west if we provide BYOK/KMS assurances. Target timeline: draft SOW/security appendix by 2026-07-02; PO targeted end of July.

Recommended negotiation posture:
- Offer a 45-day pilot under a tightened security appendix: 0-persistent-logs for the pilot, restricted access, and a joint runbook for incident debugging (they must provide redacted repros or ephemeral playback).
- Require Dedicated or Private for the pilot (we should not accept long-term hosted 0-retention concessions without platform isolation).
- Commercial offset: limited-term credit and an accelerated onboarding fee to cover private infra setup.

Action items:
1) Rishi: please prepare (a) a short security appendix draft that allows a pilot 0-retention clause with required controls (RBAC, audit hooks, ephemeral debugging process), and (b) list of what evidence we can share publicly (SOC2 redacted, pen test summary). Target: EOD Tue 16 Jun.
2) Aditya: scope effort to spin a small dedicated pool + BYOK integration estimate and timeline. Include estimated infra cost and onboarding steps. Target: Wed 17 Jun.
3) Neha: confirm whether we can provide signed redacted SOC2 and the appropriate sharing process; flag any compliance blockers for EU residency routing.

I’ll draft the email to Alex that outlines the pilot terms and proposed SOW timeline once we have Rishi’s appendix and Aditya’s infra scope.

Thanks —
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
